findings.problem: status is a public String primitive instead of a domain enum. Any string value is valid, including "", "deleted", "sent", and "pending" simultaneously with is_sent=true, making illegal states representable.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can set status to an arbitrary string that does not correspond to any valid workflow state, and the struct can encode contradictory state (e.g. status="pending" with is_sent=true). Consumers cannot exhaustively match on status, so new states silently ignored at match sites.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a sealed enum: pub enum PacketStatus { Created, Validated, Sent } with Display impl if serialization is needed. Remove is_sent entirely as the enum encodes the lifecycle.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are separate boolean lifecycle flags instead of a single typestate enum. This allows impossible combinations: is_validated=true with is_sent=true and status="created", or both false (never created vs never validated).
findings.failure_mode: The three-field representation (status String + bool + bool) has 3*2*2=12 possible state combinations, only 3 of which are valid. Any of the 9 invalid combinations can flow through the system undetected, causing silent logic errors or undefined behavior in consumers.
findings.fix: Replace all three fields with a single typestate enum: pub enum PacketTypestate { Created, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }. Remove status, is_validated, and is_sent entirely.

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts a fully owned PacketWorkflow with no state validation. It blindly sets status="sent" and is_sent=true regardless of whether the packet was previously validated, already sent, or never created.
findings.failure_mode: Any packet, regardless of its prior state, can be marked as sent. A never-validated packet transitions directly to sent. A packet already marked sent can be sent again. This violates the workflow invariant that validation must precede sending.
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with a fallible method on a typestate-aware type, e.g. fn transition_to_sent(self) -> Result<PacketWorkflow, TransitionError> that checks the current typestate and returns an error for invalid transitions.

findings.problem: All fields of PacketWorkflow are public (pub). Any caller can set status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms to any value, completely bypassing the intended workflow invariants. The struct has no constructors or methods enforcing domain rules.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can directly construct PacketWorkflow { id: "x".into(), status: "sent".into(), is_validated: false, is_sent: true, sent_at_epoch_ms: None } — an impossible state where the packet is marked sent but not validated and has no timestamp. The entire domain model is void of any invariant protection.
findings.fix: Make all fields private (remove pub). Provide a private constructor or a builder pattern that enforces invariants. Use a typestate enum for lifecycle so the compiler prevents illegal transitions.

findings.problem: item.status = "sent".to_string() allocates a new String from a string literal for a constant assignment. The String is heap-allocated every call even though the value is a static string.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation on every call to mark_sent, increasing memory pressure and GC work in hot paths. The .to_string() call is redundant — a &'static str would suffice if the field were redesigned as an enum variant.
findings.fix: Replace with a typestate enum variant (eliminates the allocation entirely). If the field must remain a String, use item.status = String::from("sent") or better yet change the field to an enum and remove this line.

findings.problem: No benchmarks exist for mark_sent or PacketWorkflow. If this function is on a hot path, there is no evidence that its allocation pattern (String::from on status field) or any future optimizations are correct.
findings.failure_mode: Without benchmark evidence, performance regressions in PacketWorkflow or mark_sent are undetectable. Any future changes to the type or function cannot be validated against a baseline.
findings.fix: Add a criterion or tinybench benchmark for mark_sent that measures allocation count and latency across a range of input packet sizes.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or PacketWorkflow hot-path performance
no profiler evidence for allocation patterns in the workflow
no second-ring evidence (assembly/SBOM) for any performance or zero-cost claims
no command evidence (cargo fmt / cargo check / cargo clippy / cargo test) was produced
residual_risk: The crate has no production unsafe, unwrap, expect, panic, or unreachable! calls. The primary risk is architectural: the type system provides zero domain invariant protection — all 9 of 12 possible state combinations are valid but incorrect. A reviewer relying solely on static grep for forbidden constructs would pass this crate; a semantic review reveals that every struct field and every function is a violation of the Holzman Rust core contract. The typestate rewrite is a prerequisite before any performance or evidence gates are meaningful.
